narratives.Overview:
# `scope:complete` synthesises `PlanItem.id` values the 0.8 schema forbids, and `xbrief:validate` passes them

Two halves, same as #4698's shape: the writer emits a value the schema rejects, and the validator that should catch it does not look.

## Measured

Consumer repo on `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.1`.

**The writer.** A brief ingested from a GitHub issue had `items: []` and three derived acceptance clauses. `scope:complete` synthesised one plan item per clause:

```json
"items": [
  { "id": "clause:1", "title": "clause:1", "status": "pending" },
  { "id": "clause:2", "title": "clause:2", "status": "pending" },
  { "id": "clause:3", "title": "clause:3", "status": "pending" }
]
```

It also reports them in its own refusal text as `items[0] «untrusted:clause:1»`.

**The schema.** `xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json`, `$defs/PlanItem/properties/id`:

```json
{ "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(\\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)*$" }
```

Dot-separated segments only. The colon is not in the class, so every synthesised id is non-conformant:

```
id='clause:1'  matches schema pattern: False
id='clause:2'  matches schema pattern: False
id='clause:3'  matches schema pattern: False
```

**The validator does not catch it.** With all three ids present:

```
$ deft xbrief:validate
OK: vBRIEF validation passed: 38 scope vBRIEF(s), PROJECT-DEFINITION
```

`verify:vbrief-conformance` also passes — it checks bare keys (#1620), not the id pattern. So `deft check` is green on an artifact that does not satisfy the shipped schema.

## How it surfaced

Not from the toolchain. A bot reviewer flagged it as P1 on the lifecycle PR, correctly citing the pattern and proposing `clause.1`. Every Directive gate in the path — commit hooks, `xbrief:validate`, `verify:vbrief-conformance`, `deft check` — was green on the colon form.

Renaming to `clause.1` / `clause.2` / `clause.3` conforms. A repo-wide sweep of every brief found no other non-conformant item ids, so this is the synthesis path specifically, not legacy data.

## Why it matters

`scope:complete` is the terminal lifecycle write. The artifact it produces is the durable record of what shipped, and it is the one a later consumer validates against the schema. A writer that emits ids its own schema forbids, guarded by a validator that does not check the constraint, means the invalid shape is only discovered by whoever validates strictly later — or by a bot reviewer, as here.

## Suggested shape

Two independent fixes:

1. **Writer** — synthesise `clause.N` (or any pattern-conformant form) in the `scope:complete` item-synthesis path. The `«untrusted:clause:N»` diagnostic label can keep its own formatting; the persisted `id` is what must conform.
2. **Validator** — have `xbrief:validate` enforce `PlanItem.id` against the schema pattern. A schema constraint that no shipped gate checks is the same gap as #4698's `KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES`: a closed set declared in one place and never consumed.

Fixing only the writer leaves the validator blind to hand-authored or older artifacts.

Related: #4697, #4698 (same writer-permissive / reader-blind shape on reference types).

## Gate stamp

The triage author stamps the semantic call. This write-back is the round-1 ceiling.

P1 is that `scope:complete` synthesises `clause:N` PlanItem ids the 0.8 schema pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)*$` forbids, and `xbrief:validate` / `verify:vbrief-conformance` do not enforce that pattern, so `deft check` is green. Consumer repo on `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.1`. Renaming to `clause.N` conforms. A repo-wide sweep found no other non-conformant item ids.

What this P1 is not:

- Not changing the `«untrusted:clause:N»` diagnostic label format.
- Not a legacy-data migration of other id shapes.
- Not treating a bot reviewer as the gate.

Suggested shape on the issue is two independent fixes: persist a pattern-conformant id, and have `xbrief:validate` enforce `PlanItem.id`. Re-measured at `19f20e3220d34258db0614d8165ab3024b85be0b`.

Round 1, fresh critic. Open critique. Ceiling 5752167698 inclusive. Re-derived at dispatch-sha `19f20e3220d34258db0614d8165ab3024b85be0b`. Process-only. No product patch.

## P1 re-measurement

The warrant holds. I tried to refute "the schema pattern is a closed constraint that no shipped gate checks" and could not.

Ran, not cited:

- 0.6, 0.8, and `packages/types` copies of PlanItem.id share one pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)*$`. `id` is optional (`required`: title, status). Node match: `clause:1` false, `clause.1` true, `github.issue.5450735782` true, `1` true.
- `validatePlanItem` uses `item.id` only to build the error path. It does not test the pattern, and it does not type-check `id`. Fixture `{ id: "clause:1", title, status }` therefore has zero schema errors from that function.
- `scanVbrief` / `ITEM_CORE` names the key `id`. It does not read the value. Conformance stays green on colon ids.
- No Ajv (or other JSON Schema engine) in `packages/**/*.ts`. The shipped consumer of schema enums is the hand-rolled walker (`VALID_PLAN_ITEM_EFFORTS`, status, type) plus `validatePlanReferenceTypes` for #4698.
- Writer: `CLAUSE_KEYED_ITEM_ID_PREFIX = "clause:"`. `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems` (complete-prep in `scope/transition.ts` when `act === "complete"`) invents `{ id, title: id, status: "pending" }`. `bindPlanItemIdsToClauses` stamps the same id onto title-matched rows at ingest and before promote. Lookup is `clauseKeyedItemId(n)` or numeric `"n"` only.
- `vbrief:validate` is on both `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` and `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`. `atomicWriteBrief` → `validateBriefForPersist` → `validateVbriefSchema`.
- `git archive` of `xbrief/` at this SHA: 139 `clause:N` items in 29 **completed** files (none in `active/`). 21 integer ids in 7 July completed files. 3343 items with no `id` (legal: optional).

Two named fixes remain the right shape. Schema-widen is a fork, not a third required fix. Recuts below are how those two fixes bind.

## Findings

### 1. The writer is the prefix constant and its lookups, not only the complete persist helper. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Production sites of `clauseKeyedItemId` / the prefix at this SHA: `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems` (complete), `bindPlanItemIdsToClauses` (ingest in `issue-ingest.ts`, promote in `promote-path.ts`), and `clauseHasKeyedItem` / `findItemByKey` (stamp, status, evidence). Re-ran the lookup: a key set `{ "clause:1" }` is not keyed under prefix `clause.`; a set `{ "clause.1" }` is not keyed under prefix `clause:`. Numeric `"1"` still matches either prefix via the existing `String(clause.id)` arm.

**Failure mode.** An implementer edits only `persistClauseKeyedPendingItems` as "the scope:complete item-synthesis path." Ingest and promote keep writing `clause:1`. Fail-closed validate then refuses those new briefs. Conversely, flipping the prefix constant without reading the old form: a leftover `clause:1` row from a complete that persisted items and then failed the acceptance gate is unbound, so the next complete invents a second row `clause.1`.

**Disposition.** Change `CLAUSE_KEYED_ITEM_ID_PREFIX` to `clause.`. Dual-read `clause:N` on lookup. On the complete persist path, rewrite an existing `clause:N` id (and a title that is exactly that id) to `clause.N` so leftover rows become persistable under the new validator. Do not treat ingest/promote bind as a second design. Do not add a parallel id mint.

### 2. Fail-closed validate cannot land as an independent second PR, and it reds this repo unless synthesis ids are rewritten. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `validateBriefForPersist` already concatenates `validateVbriefSchema`. Complete persist writes through that path. `vbrief:validate` is a `deft check` gate on this repo and on consumers. Archive walk at this SHA: 29 completed briefs, 139 `clause:N` items. #4746 is the existing "consume a closed set, corpus would go red" move: those twelve spellings warn, they do not fail-closed.

**Failure mode.** Validator-only: persist still emits `clause:1`, `atomicWriteBrief` refuses, complete cannot persist items. Validator-with-writer but no corpus rewrite: `vbrief:validate` on `check:framework-source` fails on those 29 files, so the PR cannot merge here. Ajv-against-the-JSON-file would also fail the 21 integer ids (schema `type: string`) and is a new engine.

**Disposition.** Same unit of work: writer first or together, then pattern check on **string** `id` when present, inside `validatePlanItem` next to effort/status (reuse `constants` the way `VALID_PLAN_ITEM_EFFORTS` is reused). Same-PR rewrite of synthesis-emitted `clause:N` in this corpus. Integer ids stay a leftover, not P1, unless a later lean names schema `type`. Warn-first à la #4746 is the alternative if rewrite is refused; it is not the default. Do not plug Ajv. Do not put the check in `scanVbrief`. Do not make `id` required.

## Road not taken

Chose consume-the-pattern, not schema-widen (allow `:` in the class).

Steelmanned rejected: colon is already a delimiter in `«untrusted:…»` and in GitHub-style labels, so widening is cheaper than 139 rewrites. Flip condition: the shipped 0.6/0.8 pattern is dotted segments, and plan-id mint already uses that shape (`github.issue.<n>`). Widening is a schema recut that also has to decide whether `:` is a segment character or a second separator. #4698 consumed the closed set; it did not enlarge it. I would flip if a documented PlanItem.id contract said opaque tokens, not dotted segments.

## Footnotes

- `fenceUntrustedAcceptanceText` wraps **title**, and persist sets `title` to the id. After `clause.N`, refuse listings show `«untrusted:clause.N»`. No separate colon formatter to preserve. The fence itself is not a schema field.
- Tests at this SHA hard-code `clause:1` (`acceptance-evidence.test.ts`, `issue-ingest.test.ts`, `completed-write-guard.test.ts`). Expected recut with the prefix, not extra design.
- Injection / swarm lens: not applied. This is a writer/validator schema-pattern gap, not an authority or envelope change.
